verdict: Coconut water has roughly one third of the calories of sugarcane juice. Sugarcane juice is still okay, just drink a small size and only once in a while.
why: Sugarcane juice is an estimated 180 kcal per glass, coconut water around 60 kcal. A 120 kcal difference.
Both have almost no protein (0 g vs 1 g), so neither helps much with fullness.
Almost all the calories in sugarcane juice come from natural sugar. The calories are the same as other sweet drinks.
Sugarcane juice is cold and sweet, so it's easy to finish a big glass on a hot night at the pasar malam.
when_a: Sugarcane juice is okay when you share a glass, or get a small size while walking around the pasar malam.
when_b: Coconut water suits hot weather when you want a refreshing, lighter drink.
tip: Ask for sugarcane juice with lots of ice and a squeeze of lime, or choose coconut water with no added sugar. Drink plain water first to quench your thirst.

faq.q: The sugar in sugarcane juice is natural, so it's fine, right?
faq.a: Natural sugar still has calories. Sugarcane juice can fit in your diet, just control the size and how often.

faq.q: Can I drink coconut water every day?
faq.a: Yes, in moderate amounts. Make sure the seller doesn't add sugar or syrup.
